User-facing Latin spelling follows PUJL (Balai Bahasa Yogyakarta). Predecessors: Wewaton Sriwedari 1926 and Pedoman Penulisan Aksara Jawa 2002. See docs/references/CITATIONS.md in the repository.

deviationTitle: How this differs from the traditional order
deviationBody: The traditional order (Kongres Aksara Jawa I Yogyakarta 2021; see the About page) teaches the 20 nglegena letters row by row (ha na ca ra ka, da ta sa wa la, and so on) and introduces sandhangan only after all of them. This app differs in two ways. First, the nglegena letters are grouped by similar shape, the way Latin letters are taught in shape families (i l j, then r b p d). Letters that look alike are learned side by side, from simple shapes to complex ones. This grouping follows a teacher's suggestion and is still under review. Second, wulu (i) and suku (u) are pulled forward, straight after the first group pa ha ya. Without sandhangan every syllable sounds as a consonant + /a/, so a pupil can read very few words; with wulu and suku the vocabulary widens at once.
unitOrderBody:
1. Group 1: pa ha ya
2. wulu (i) and suku (u) — pulled forward
3. Group 2: ra ga la
4. Group 3: na ka ca sa
5. Group 4: da dha ja ta wa
6. Group 5: ba nga tha nya ma
7. remaining sandhangan
8. pasangan
9. advanced wing: murda and swara
Rekan, angka and pada are in the free-roam chart, ungated.
reviewHelpWhyBody: Memory fades fast. A short review just before you forget makes the letters stick — and every success stretches the gap: 10 minutes, then 1, 3, 8, 20 days.
reviewHelpGradeAgain: Ulangi — you missed it: see it again now, then again in 10 minutes.
reviewHelpGradeHard: Agak sulit — you got it but struggled: back tomorrow.
reviewHelpGradeGood: Lancar — smooth: tomorrow, then less and less often.
reviewHelpGradeEasy: Mudah — too easy: in 6 days, then faster.
